# Check of phase 5 against the instrument error of armlib.run_jobs (read-only; generated by `check_phase5_timeouts.py`)

## Code

Words of the old instrument error searched in the harness files: `phase5.py`: none; `phase5s.py`: none; `phase5c.py`: none; `phase5_engine.py`: none. No phase 5 file imports `armlib` or has a restart loop. A run is one `H.run_task` in a thread of one process; every run opens its own engine on its own copy of the base store (`E.open_run`, a directory per run). A tool call that gets no answer within the engine timeout raises `EngineTimeout`; `run_task` catches it, records `engine_timeout` and `harness_error` on THAT run and closes it; the process goes on with the next run on its own engine copy. `os._exit` is called only after every job of the command has finished (`ex.map` returned), so it cannot end a job that was still to run.

Ledger against the records: each cell's ledger entry equals the sum of its run records' cost except in one Haiku pg cell, whose entry also counts the second canary (three runs that are not in the table). So every attempt that was recorded was ledgered and the other way round; an attempt that raised `HarnessError` before it was recorded would leave no trace in either, and the cell logs I can read (the 12 cells and the re-run) hold no `HARNESS ERROR`, `Traceback` or `stopped early` line. I found no log of the `sql_script` cells to read.

## Isolation of a timeout (offline replay with the stub model, task R1 on the pg arm, two runs in one process)

- an engine timeout of 0.0005 s: engine_timeout True, success False, calls 1.
- the normal timeout: engine_timeout False, success True, calls 2.

The run with the tiny timeout is flagged and fails; the next run in the same process, on its own engine copy, is untouched and succeeds. A timeout therefore cannot turn the next job into a lost one in this harness.
